title: Adaptive priority gating and collaboration flow for enterprise access requests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customer enterprise teams frequently submit admin & access requests (RBAC role templates, SSO/SAML integrations, SCIM provisioning rules, organization-wide policy exceptions). These requests vary widely in urgency and risk; our current intake is manual and inconsistent, causing slow response for high-risk items and unnecessary escalations for low-risk ones. Goal: Build an adaptive triage flow that automatically classifies and gates incoming enterprise admin/access requests into priority lanes, surfaces required approvers and data, and provides a collaborative checklist for PM/Engineering/Support/Customer Success. The flow should reduce time-to-resolution for high-impact requests, prevent priority inversion, and improve handoff quality for engineering and security reviews. Scope: Non-bug admin & access requests only (onboarding, RBAC changes, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org policy exceptions). Excludes incident/production outages and feature requests unrelated to access. Deliverables: 1) scoring heuristic and gating thresholds, 2) intake form adjustments and required fields, 3) automated routing rules (email/Slack/Linear), 4) a short runbook for reviewers, 5) metrics dashboard and SLA targets.
acceptance_criteria: All incoming enterprise admin/access requests are assigned a numeric triage score and mapped to a priority lane (P0/P1/P2) using the defined heuristic.
Intake form enforces required evidence fields for high-risk scores (eg. data classification, regulatory scope, org size, customer_tier).
Automated routing sends high-risk, high-priority requests to Security + Solutions Eng + PM within 30 minutes and low-risk to Support queue.
Reviewers see an inline checklist in Linear ticket with required approvers and expected SLA for each lane.
Dashboard shows median time-to-first-response and time-to-resolution by lane; initial targets: median TTF response P0 < 1h, P1 < 4h, P2 < 48h.
Pilot with three enterprise customers for 4 weeks with improved resolution times and qualitative feedback from CS teams.
proposed_flow_steps: 1) Request submission from customer portal/Support with enhanced intake form (fields: customer_tier, change_type, data_sensitivity, need_by_date, org_size, existing_integrations, business_impact).
2) Auto-compute triage score using scoring formula and append tags to Linear ticket.
3) Gate: If score >= 80 -> Priority P0 (manual approvers required), 50-79 -> P1 (expedited review), <50 -> P2 (standard).
4) Auto-route: P0 -> Security Slack channel + assign ENG and PM; P1 -> Solutions Eng + PM; P2 -> Support queue with CS notification.
5) Reviewer checklist and required artifacts appear as comments/template in the ticket; reviewers mark items and add time estimates for work.
6) If dependencies on infra/feature work are detected, create linked ENG sub-issue and set follow-up SLA for handoff.
7) After decision, post structured response to customer and update customer-facing status page if needed.
scoring_formula: Base score components (weights): customer_tier (VIP=30, Enterprise=20, Standard=5), data_sensitivity (High=30, Medium=15, Low=0), regulatory_scope (GDPR/HIPAA/PIPEDA=20), org_size (>1000=10, 100-1000=5), outage_risk (potential service impact=25), requested_changes_radius (org-wide=15, team=5).
Example: VIP (30) + High data sensitivity (30) + GDPR (20) + org_size 500 (5) + outage_risk 0 + org-wide 15 = 100 -> P0.
Thresholds: >=80 P0, 50-79 P1, <50 P2. Allow manual override with required justification logged in ticket.
Auto-escalation: if request waits > SLA for lane without assignee, escalate to on-call and PM.
notes: We should coordinate with CS & Support for messaging and with Security for the approval matrix. This is intentionally conservative for the pilot; thresholds can be relaxed after 8 weeks of telemetry. Plan includes a manual override path for urgent customer deadlines (requires 2 approvers).
